search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Legionnaires' disease cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and outbreak events in Ontario, Canada during July 2025 (2025-07-01 to 2025-07-31). Priority sources are Public Health Ontario, local public health units, Health Canada, and credible news outlets covering Ontario health events.
search_reasoning: The upstream plan contains 10 queries across 5 channels but uses overly rigid quoted phrase constructions (e.g., "Legionnaires disease Ontario 2025" as a single quoted phrase) that are likely to return zero results because such exact strings are unlikely to appear verbatim in official reports or news articles. The time-range string "2025-07-01-2025-07-31" embedded in query text is also non-standard and will not match real documents. Additionally, the upstream queries do not leverage Ontario-specific agency naming (Public Health Ontario, local health units such as Toronto Public Health, Ottawa Public Health, etc.) or disease-specific surveillance terminology used in Canadian public health reporting (e.g., "iPHIS", "reportable disease", "Legionellosis"). Given the 4-query-per-iteration cap, this first iteration prioritizes: (1) a refined official/public-health web search targeting Public Health Ontario and local health units with natural-language terms; (2) a news search for July 2025 Ontario Legionnaires' coverage; (3) a structured-database/surveillance query targeting PHAC and Ontario reportable disease data; and (4) a ProMED/international alert query for Ontario Legionella signals. Peer-reviewed literature is deprioritized for iteration 1 because a July 2025 outbreak would not yet have published papers.

query_batch.query: Legionnaires disease Ontario July 2025 cases outbreak public health
query_batch.query_rationale: Targets Public Health Ontario, local health unit websites, and Health Canada pages using natural-language terms without over-rigid quoting. 'July 2025' is more likely to match real document text than a date-range string. Covers both 'Legionnaires disease' and 'outbreak' to capture surveillance bulletins, health alerts, and reportable disease summaries.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Public Health Ontario situation reports, local health unit advisories, Health Canada reportable disease tables, Ontario health alerts
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Domain from ontario.ca, publichealthontario.ca, canada.ca, or named local health unit (.ca domain); official report language such as 'confirmed cases', 'reportable disease', 'health unit'

query_batch.query: Legionella outbreak Ontario 2025 cases deaths hospitalizations health unit
query_batch.query_rationale: News outlets (CBC, CTV, Toronto Star, Ottawa Citizen, local Ontario papers) frequently report on Legionella outbreaks with case counts, death tolls, and locality details before official surveillance summaries are published. Using 'health unit' anchors results to Ontario-specific reporting structures. Avoids over-quoted phrases that suppress relevant results.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CBC News, CTV News, Toronto Star, Ottawa Citizen, Hamilton Spectator, or other Ontario regional news articles reporting case counts, deaths, or outbreak investigations
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Named journalist or news outlet, dateline in July 2025, reference to a named public health official or health unit, specific case or death count

query_batch.query: Public Health Ontario Legionellosis reportable disease surveillance 2025
query_batch.query_rationale: Public Health Ontario publishes reportable disease data through its integrated Public Health Information System (iPHIS) and annual/quarterly infectious disease summaries. 'Legionellosis' is the formal reportable disease name used in Ontario surveillance. This query targets structured data tables or downloadable datasets that may include July 2025 case counts by health unit.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Public Health Ontario infectious disease query (IDQR) tool, Ontario reportable disease data tables, PHAC notifiable disease database entries for Ontario
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: publichealthontario.ca or canada.ca domain, tabular case count data, reference to iPHIS or PHAC notifiable disease surveillance system

query_batch.query_rationale: ProMED-mail (Program for Monitoring Emerging Diseases) is an authoritative international disease alert system that frequently posts early signals of Legionella outbreaks in Canada, including Ontario. ProMED posts often cite local health authority statements and include case/death counts. This complements official agency searches and may surface July 2025 alerts not yet indexed in official databases.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: ProMED-mail alert post referencing Ontario Legionella cases or outbreak, with case counts and source attribution to a Canadian health authority
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: promedmail.org domain, ISID affiliation, post date in 2025, reference to Ontario health unit or PHAC

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong signals of a confirmed Legionnaires' disease outbreak in the Middlesex-London Health Unit area of Ontario during July 2025, with multiple case-count and death-count data points visible in snippets (66 cases/2 deaths as of July 14; 70 cases/2 deaths as of July 29; 94 cases/4 deaths at a later re-declaration; ~100 total per CBC). However, several critical gaps remain: (1) The Middlesex-London Health Unit's own official outbreak update pages beyond July 14 have not been directly surfaced (only one healthunit.com result appeared); (2) The Public Health Ontario 2025 surveillance PDF is the single most authoritative source but only snippets are available — additional PHO situation reports or interim bulletins may exist; (3) The govdelivery.com result (likely a health unit email alert) and outbreaknewstoday.substack.com result were accepted but not summarized — these may contain dated case counts; (4) The canada.ca results were not summarized and may contain PHAC notifiable disease data for Ontario July 2025; (5) The outbreak timeline spans late June through at least late July, so additional dated status updates (July 21, July 28, July 31) from the Middlesex-London Health Unit are likely to exist and would provide time-series case/death data within the July 2025 window; (6) The beaconbio.org results reference a Toronto cluster in 2026 (out of scope) and a London Ontario event — these need disambiguation; (7) No ProMED-specific result was surfaced, suggesting that channel may not have returned results. Iteration 2 should focus on: (a) Middlesex-London Health Unit direct outbreak update pages for all July 2025 status updates; (b) PHAC/canada.ca notifiable disease data for Ontario; (c) Additional news coverage with specific dated case counts (CBC London, London Free Press, CTV London); (d) The govdelivery/content.govdelivery result which likely is a health unit email alert with precise counts.

MLHU typically publishes multiple dated status updates during an active outbreak (e.g., July 7, July 21, July 28, July 31). This query targets the MLHU news/updates section directly to surface all July 2025 outbreak status pages, which will provide the time-series case and death counts needed for the July 2025 window.
